title: Adaptive Hosted Endpoint PRD and Progressive Launch Checklist
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines an "adaptive" hosted inference endpoint bundle that unifies chat/completions/embeddings/rerank behaviors under a single, predictable contract and a progressive launch plan. The emphasis is production-readiness: latency SLOs per plan, deterministic fallback behavior, model-compatibility guarantees, and automatic quality gates driven by small evaluation suites (golden prompts + fuzz tests).

Goals:
- Provide a single API surface that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank with clear behavioral defaults and opt-in advanced behaviors.
- Ensure stable latency (p50/p95) and cost envelopes across workload profiles with automated routing and quantization recommendations.
- Ship a progressive rollout (canary -> regional -> global) with automated rollback and regression detection tied to prompt-based evals.

Non-goals:
- We do not attempt to merge multimodal assets in this scope.
- No on-prem packaging changes; Private mode compatibility covered in a follow-up.

Key requirements (product + acceptance-focused):
1) API surface: single /v2/infer endpoint with mode parameter (chat|complete|embed|rerank). Backwards-compatible feature flags for existing endpoints must be supported for 6 months.
2) Behavioral defaults: chat uses conversation-aware stop sequences, completions default to top-p:0.95 and temperature:0.2, embeddings return normalized float32 vectors and an explicit model_id in metadata.
3) Quality gates: for each model variant supported at launch, we will run a 250-prompt golden set (customer- and generic prompts) and require no more than 3% drop in intent-preservation and a BLEU/ROUGE threshold where applicable.
4) Latency & SLOs: p50 <= 60ms (small tokens), p95 <= 300ms for baseline plans on hosted capacity. If SLO violation > 5% for 15m, automated fallback to compatible model variant or region.
5) Cost controls: endpoint must honor per-tenant rate limits and a soft budget throttle; SDKs expose a "cost_estimate" header in responses.
6) Observability: token-level cost/time, per-model counters, latency histograms, and a rollout health dashboard must be available.

Scope clarifications / trade-offs:
- Batching: continuous batching enabled by default; customers can opt-out for ultra-low latency. Batching logic will prefer throughput for embeddings.
- Rerank integration: rerank will be exposed as a first-class sub-mode that accepts candidate lists; heavy candidate sets (>100) will be queued for background scoring with explicit job IDs.
- Model fallback: small-model fallbacks (quantized variants) may produce slightly different outputs; a compatibility contract document must list known deterministic differences.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- API contract verified by automated contract tests against SDKs (node/python) with 100% pass.
- Golden-set regression: for each model and plan, run golden prompts before and after rollout; no regression beyond threshold.
- Load test: sustained 1k rps traffic with representative mix (chat 50%, embed 30%, complete 15%, rerank 5%) without p95 SLO breaches in our staging cluster.
- Rollout automation: a canary with 2% traffic routing that can be promoted or rolled back via the console or API in under 2 minutes.
- Observability: dashboard populates within 2 mins of traffic; alerts fire for latency/cost anomalies and for quality gate failures.

Launch checklist (progressive):
Pre-launch (engineering + PM + DX):
- [ ] API spec published to docs and SDKs updated with examples for each mode.
- [ ] Open-source quickstart sample app demonstrating chat + rerank + embeddings.
- [ ] Golden prompt set curated (internal + 50 anonymized customer prompts) and evaluation harness wired to CI.
- [ ] Compatibility contract doc published listing model variants and known output deltas.
- [ ] Security review completed and KMS keys validated for telemetry and logs.
- [ ] Billing/cost estimation fields validated and rate-limit defaults set per plan.
Staged rollout (canary -> regional -> global):
- [ ] Canary: 2% traffic in us-west with real telemetry enabled for 24h; automatic quality checks run every hour.
- [ ] Regional: expand to 10% in two additional regions, run 48h validation.
- [ ] Global: 100% gradual rollout with monitored ramp; full validation for 7 days.
Launch day ops readiness:
- [ ] Runbook: on-call escalation path and rollback steps documented (console revert + API action + traffic-split change).
- [ ] Run a simulated incident drill (latency spike + quality regression) with on-call.
- [ ] Post-launch evaluation plan: daily golden-set runs first week, weekly thereafter.

Monitoring & KPIs:
- Latency p50/p95 per mode and per plan.
- Token cost and token rate per tenant.
- Quality gate pass rate for golden prompts per model.
- Error rate and tail error classes (OOM, timeouts, kernel errors).
- Rollout health: % traffic on new endpoint vs stability baseline.

Dependencies:
- Runtime 2.0 kernel selection changes (ENG-51021).
- Console rollout automation API (ENG-49802).
- SDK bump with new mode parameter (DX-1120).

Fallback & mitigation plan:
- When quality gate fails in canary, trigger automatic rollback to previous model variant and open a regression ticket with logs, diff artifacts, and sample prompts.
- If latency SLOs breach in a region for >30m, shift traffic to alternate region and notify customers using status page.

Open decisions (for PM + Eng):
- Acceptable regression threshold per model family for embeddings (cosine similarity delta). Proposal: 0.02 mean delta across gold set.
- Long-term plan for deprecating old endpoints and migration window length.

Docs & artifacts links:
- API spec (internal): https://docs.internal.redwood/api/infer-v2
- Evaluation harness (CI): https://ci.redwood/evals/hosted-endpoints
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/endpoint-launch

Notes & follow-ups:
- Schedule a post-mortem window 72h after global launch to collect customer feedback and identify immediate QoS improvements.
- PM will coordinate with Solutions for enterprise pilot customers to run private canaries.
